post.summary: Add an exam to a course
post.description: An exam page (a course exam) is a name and the course's folders on it, shared by everyone like the folders. A folder is on one exam page at most: a folder of another page is refused with 409, naming it ("First Pass is in Exam 2."), as is a second page with the same name, and a folder whose name another folder on the page already has ("Exam 3 already has a folder named First Pass."). A folder taken off the page goes back to the end of the course's Folders list, refused with 409 when a folder there has its name. A folder id or name the course does not have is refused with 400. Her past exams belong to the page holding every folder they were over (ExamSummary.courseExamId). The student and the admin can both do this.

201.description: The new exam, after the course's other exams.

put.summary: Rename an exam page and set its folders

A folder taken off the page goes back to the end of the course's Folders list, refused with 409 when a folder there has its name. A folder id or name the course does not have is refused with 400. Her past exams belong to the page holding every folder they were over (ExamSummary.courseExamId). The student and the admin can both do this. The folders sent replace the page's folders, in the order sent.

A clash is refused with 409, naming the list ("Exam 3 already has a folder named First Pass.", "NURS 402 already has a folder named Second Pass."). Two pages may each have a folder of the same name. The student and the admin can both do this.

The student and the admin can both do this. Renaming it to its own name, or putting it on the page it is on, changes nothing.

Its questions may name their practice twin in `twinOf`: the id of a practice question in the same folder. A set conflicts only with a current set of the same kind and name in the course. A replace keeps the set in its folder, whatever folder the import names.

Then her running exam in this course and her ended exams, newest first. An exam whose time has run out is ended first. The admin reads the same, read-only. Then what every exam follows (`rules`), what each exam page would draw (`courseExams`), and, when `folderIds` (or legacy `weeks`) are given, what starting an exam over them would draw (`preview`), worked out as POST does.

post.summary: Start an exam over the folders she ticked
post.description: Draws up to 40 questions only from the sets in the ticked folders, in proportion to each folder's size, with 60 minutes for 40 or 1.5 minutes per question when the folders hold fewer. A folder with an exam bank gives its exam-bank questions; a folder without one gives its practice questions, and once the course has any exam bank the exam lists such folders in practiceWeeks. With pool `wrong`, only the questions she last answered not fully right are drawn: practice questions, exam-bank questions, and the exam twins of practice questions she got wrong (the one practice question of the same folder whose id the exam question names in twinOf) until she answers the twin fully right; a ticked folder with none is refused with `no_wrong_questions`. Send `folderIds`, or legacy `weeks` (folder names, each meaning every folder of that name), not both; with neither, it is refused with `no_folders`. A folder the course does not have is refused with `folder_not_found`, one with no questions with `folder_empty`, and a name no folder with questions has with `week_not_found`. A running exam of hers ends first. Answers go to POST /api/attempts with this exam's id as studySessionId. The admin cannot start one.

get.description: Its questions in the order served and the ones she has answered. Once it has ended, the result: points, fully right, partly right, missed, guessed, not answered, minutes used, the by-folder, by-week and by-clinical-judgment-step breakdowns, each question's mark, how many practice questions went to Review, and how many exam-bank questions she got wrong (they stay out of Review). An exam whose time has run out is ended first.

post.summary: End her exam and score it
post.description: `finished` when she finishes, `left` when she leaves midway, `timeout` when her time runs out. What she answered is scored; skipped and unreached questions score 0 and stay out of Review. After the time limit the end is recorded as a timeout. Ending an ended exam returns it unchanged. The admin cannot call this.

200.description: The ended exam with its result.
